text:
ana: FYI i traced an eviction cascade last night; root cause looks like control-plane commit batching + clients assuming leases are durable. we need a clearer surface for in-flight renewals.
ryan: agreed. the current pin object only has ttl + last_updated which is ambiguous when commits are batched. clients can't tell if a renewal is assured.
sam: what if we add a small state machine on the pin metadata? e.g. `lease_phase` enum: {"active", "renewing", "committed", "expired"} and a `lease_nonce` string (opaque) that changes on every commit. clients compare cached nonce->server nonce to detect staleness.
ana (ops-bot): note: we tried a similar approach with multipart-commit in 2024 and it reduced double-allocs.
ryan: nonce + phase is nice. also add `epoch_ms` (server commit time) to help with clock skew heuristics.
sam: client policy proposal: if lease_phase == "renewing" and time_until_epoch < safety_margin_ms then force re-resolve. safety_margin_ms should be small (default 3000ms) but configurable per tenant.
nana (ops-bot): remember security: lease_nonce needs to be unguessable and rotated; treat it like an HMAC over (tenant,pin,epoch).
ryan: another signal: `provenance_tags` (list) so we can see whether a renewal came from autoscaler / manual / canary. keep as strings for now.
sam: sample metadata payload we'd add to rollout API docs:
```json
{
  "lease_phase": "renewing",
  "lease_nonce": "n_3a7f9...",
  "epoch_ms": "1710000000123",
  "soft_margin_ms": "3000",
  "provenance_tags": ["autoscaler","canary-42"],
  "issuer_type": "scheduler"
}
```
ryan: naming suggestions: prefer `epoch_ms` over human durations so clients can do math without parsing. `soft_margin_ms` is clearer than safety_delta.
nana (ops-bot): metrics to emit: nonce_mismatch_count, renewing_near_epoch_count, phase_transitions_by_issuer. we can add dashboards.
sam: rollout plan: 1) emit fields read-only for 10 days, 2) release client lib changes that check nonce+phase, 3) enable GC behavior to consult `lease_phase` semantics behind a feature flag.
ryan: tests: add a chaos test that injects a 2s commit delay and ensures client fallback doesn't cascade; add time-skewed client scenarios.
nana (ops-bot): backward compat: clients must treat absent lease_nonce as unknown and prefer re-resolve; absent lease_phase default to "committed" to avoid unnecessary re-resolves.
sam: tradeoffs: this adds churn in metadata size and more signals to maintain but is much safer than tweaking TTL heuristics only.
ryan: agree. also consider a `preferred_client_behavior` hint: {"prefer_resolve","allow_stale"} so we can opt tenants into aggressive safety.
nana (ops-bot): deploy-bot: canary scheduled 2026-04-05 04:00 UTC for 5% traffic on branch `lease-meta-phase`.
